about: Street backdrop for ?v2: Cycles panoramas of NEW_exterior (room.blend, approved dusk setup) from one bake eye; see src/scene/exteriorBackdrop.ts and blender/scripts/v2_exterior_web.py.
coordinates: three.js Y-up metres; three (x, y, z) = Blender (x, z, -y). *_blender fields are Blender Z-up.
camera_basis: Equirectangular from `eye`: azimuth = atan2(x, -z) in three (Blender atan2(x, y)), + to the right of the -Z (Blender +Y) view; elevation = asin(y). u = (az - lon0)/(lon1 - lon0), v = (el - lat0)/(lat1 - lat0), v = 0 is the bottom image row. lon/lat in degrees.

encoding.decode: L = t > 0.5/255 ? 2^(min + t*(max-min)) : 0 per channel; alpha straight (back: opaque)

radiance: Scene-linear Rec.709 radiance, as Cycles wrote it before the view transform. The approved grade is applied at runtime: AgX (Blender look Medium High Contrast), exposure +0.45 EV (toneMappingExposure 2^0.45). Unlit/emissive: never lit again.

render.note: data is pre-view-transform linear; exposure/look not baked in

glass.about: The approved stills see the street through Mesh_11, a single-sided IOR 1.5 Principled glass plane (not thin-walled) at Blender y = 1.398: every view ray refracts once and never exits, magnifying the street ~1.5x. The runtime reproduces it by refracting the view ray at this plane (three z = -1.398) and applying Fresnel transmittance; ior 1 = a plain opening. The layers themselves are baked without the glass.
